requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1
requirements.summary: PV/VG/LV (vgdata/lvdata) created on a loopback-backed device (no spare block device existed on node1), formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/data, confirmed via df -h and lsblk output showing /dev/mapper/vgdata-lvdata mounted at /srv/data.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2GB while it stays mounted and its contents stay intact
requirements.summary: A second loopback PV was added to the VG and lvextend -L 2200M -r performed an online resize (resize2fs run in-place, 'on-line resizing required' message, filesystem never unmounted). Post-grow df -h confirms 2.1G size, and sha256sum -c against checksums recorded before the grow confirms both testfile.txt and blob.bin are unchanged.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently evidenced: a logical volume (vgdata/lvdata) was created and mounted at /srv/data, then grown online from 1000M to 2.15G while remaining mounted, with pre/post sha256 checksums confirming data integrity. The independently mandated node-restart evidence protocol was also executed cleanly (pre-restart baseline, reboot acknowledgement, connection-refused confirming downtime, changed boot_id, and full post-restart recovery of the LV, mount, and data), consistent with the fixed lifecycle boot-identity observations. No unnecessary or unresolved mutations were found beyond those needed to accomplish the task and its persistence/restart verification.
limitations: The public task contract does not require surviving a reboot, so the systemd unit/fstab persistence work and the restart demonstration are supporting evidence for hygiene and for the independent restart protocol, not scored as a material task outcome.

Loop device backing files (disk1.img, disk2.img) remain under /var/lib/lvm-backing as permanent storage for the LV; this is an accepted and necessary substitute given the node had no spare block device, not unmanaged residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task or to necessary prerequisites: loopback files/devices were required substitutes for a physical block device; the systemd oneshot unit and fstab entry were needed to make the loop-backed LV persist and reactivate, which was itself exercised and verified by the mandated restart protocol. One unit file was revised mid-session (cmd-1cd1a0bd26ce46f2) after diagnostics (cmd-3e60994f1019496e, cmd-a086aab5f1d34dc0) probed for an ordering-cycle risk; the revision is a reasonable corrective refinement of the same in-progress unit rather than an abandoned experiment, and it was left in a working, verified state (unit ran successfully both before and after reboot). No failed services, no unexpected listening sockets, and no dpkg/package-health regressions appear in the after_executor snapshot; the only diffs versus after_prepare are the expected boot-id change and ephemeral systemd-private tmp directories from the reboot itself. The reboot used for the mandated restart-evidence protocol was bounded and its purpose (proving persistence) is directly supported by the retained systemd unit and fstab entry.
